chunks.title: RBI KYC Master Direction — Customer Due Diligence & Officially Valid Documents (OVDs)
chunks.section: Chapter VI, Part I, Paragraph 16 — Customer Due Diligence (CDD) Procedure in Case of Individuals; Chapter I, Section 3(a)(xiv) — Officially Valid Document
chunks.description: Specifies Officially Valid Documents (OVDs) for Customer Due Diligence of individuals and provides for accepted documentation where a name change occurred subsequent to issuance.
chunks.text: For undertaking Customer Due Diligence (CDD) of individual customers, Regulated Entities (REs) shall obtain proof of possession of Aadhaar number or any Officially Valid Document (OVD) containing details of identity and address, or equivalent electronic document, along with PAN or Form 60. Officially Valid Documents include Passport, Driving Licence, Proof of possession of Aadhaar number, Voter's Identity Card, NREGA job card, or letter issued by the National Population Register. A document shall be deemed to be an OVD even if there is a change in the name subsequent to its issuance, provided it is supported by a marriage certificate issued by the State Government or a Gazette notification indicating such change of name.
chunks.applicability: RBI-regulated entities; customer identification and Customer Due Diligence (CDD) of individual customers

chunks.title: RBI KYC Master Direction — Customer Acceptance, Fictitious Names & Identification Authenticity
chunks.section: Chapter III, Paragraph 10(a)-(b) & Chapter V, Paragraph 13(c) — Customer Acceptance Policy and Customer Identification Procedure
chunks.description: Prohibits accounts in fictitious/benami names, requires non-reliability evaluation of furnished documents, and mandates identification procedures when doubts exist regarding authenticity of customer data.
chunks.text: Under the Customer Acceptance Policy and Customer Identification Procedure, Regulated Entities (REs) shall ensure that no account is opened in anonymous or fictitious/benami name, and no account is opened where the RE is unable to apply appropriate Customer Due Diligence (CDD) measures due to non-reliability of documents or information furnished. Further, REs shall undertake customer identification procedures whenever there is a doubt about the authenticity or adequacy of customer identification data obtained. Where PAN is obtained, it shall be verified through the verification facility of the issuing authority. Rejection of onboarding must not be without application of mind, and reasons for rejection shall be duly recorded.

chunks.title: RBI Master Direction on Credit Information Reporting — Reporting Standards & Credit Appraisal
chunks.section: Chapter II, Section 4 & Chapter III, Section 5 — Membership, Data Quality & Credit Information Usage
chunks.description: Mandates Credit Institution membership in all Credit Information Companies (CICs), standard reporting of credit records, and utilization of credit reports for credit appraisal.
chunks.text: Under the Reserve Bank of India (Credit Information Reporting) Directions, 2025, all Credit Institutions (CIs) are required to become members of all Credit Information Companies (CICs) registered with the RBI. CIs shall report comprehensive borrower credit records in uniform credit reporting formats, maintain high data quality index standards, and utilize credit information reports for credit appraisal and borrower indebtedness evaluation.
chunks.applicability: Credit Institutions (commercial banks, cooperative banks, NBFCs, HFCs, ARCs) and Credit Information Companies (CICs)

chunks.title: RBI Guidelines on Fair Practices Code for Lenders — Loan Processing and Reason Communication
chunks.section: Guidelines on Fair Practices Code for Lenders, Clause 2(a) — Applications for loans and their processing
chunks.description: Mandates clear disclosures on loan applications, timely collection of additional documentation, and written communication of the main reason(s) in the event of loan rejection.
chunks.text: Under the Fair Practices Code for Lenders, loan application forms shall be comprehensive and transparent regarding fees and terms. Lenders shall establish a system for acknowledging receipt of loan applications. If additional information or documentation is required from the applicant, the lender shall inform the customer promptly. In the event that a loan application is rejected after consideration, the lender shall convey in writing the main reason or reasons that led to the rejection of the loan application.

chunks.section: Annex I, Clause 1.1 — Loan Disbursal, Servicing and Repayment
chunks.description: Mandates that all digital loan disbursals and repayments occur directly between the borrower's bank account and the Regulated Entity without third-party pass-through or pool accounts.
chunks.text: Regulated Entities (REs) shall ensure that all loan disbursements and repayments are executed strictly and directly between the bank account of the borrower and the RE. Disbursals and repayments shall not pass through any pass-through account or pool account of any third party, including Lending Service Providers (LSPs) or Digital Lending Apps (DLAs), ensuring a direct, auditable fund flow.

chunks.title: HDFC Bank Personal Loan — Public Documentation Checklist for Salaried Applicants
chunks.section: Personal Loan Eligibility & Documents — Required Documents for Salaried Individuals
chunks.description: Public documentation checklist published by HDFC Bank specifying required documents for non-pre-approved salaried applicants.
chunks.text: Under HDFC Bank's publicly published personal loan checklist, salaried applicants applying through standard (non-pre-approved) channels are typically required to submit: 1) Identity Proof (Aadhaar Card, Passport, Voter ID, Driving Licence, or PAN Card); 2) Address Proof; 3) Income Proof (latest 3 months salary slips or latest Form 16); and 4) Bank Statements for the latest 3–6 months reflecting regular salary credits. Pre-approved existing customers may be eligible for digital processing with no physical documentation required.

chunks.title: HDFC Bank Personal Loan — Public Credit Score & Repayment Guidance
chunks.section: Personal Loan Guidance — Credit Score & Eligibility Overview
chunks.description: Public guidance published by HDFC Bank regarding the role of credit score (CIBIL), repayment track record, and credit utilization for loan eligibility.
chunks.text: HDFC Bank publicly advises personal loan applicants that credit score (CIBIL) and past credit history are key factors in evaluating creditworthiness. Applicants with higher credit scores (typically 720–750 and above) have higher approval probability and may secure favorable loan terms. The bank emphasizes maintaining a consistent track record of on-time EMI and credit card payments, keeping credit card utilization low (ideally under 30%), and avoiding multiple concurrent loan applications.

chunks.section: Underwriting Policy Part 2.3 — Income Variance Threshold
chunks.description: Simulated demo rule establishing variance limits between payslip net income and bank statement credits.
chunks.text: [SIMULATED DEMO RULE] A variance greater than 10.0% between the net salary stated on the payslip and the average monthly salary credit observed in the bank statement constitutes a financial discrepancy. Moderate discrepancies require underwriting clarification (STANDARD_REVIEW with note), whereas variances exceeding 25% or multiple conflicting records require OFFICER_INVESTIGATION.

chunks.title: Simulated Bank Rule — Critical Identity Mismatch Zero-Tolerance Policy
chunks.section: Fraud Prevention & KYC Part 3.1 — Primary Identity Mismatch
chunks.description: Simulated demo rule requiring immediate officer escalation when loan application name does not match KYC identity.
chunks.text: [SIMULATED DEMO RULE] When the primary applicant name on the loan application form does not match the name extracted from the government KYC document (Aadhaar/PAN/Voter ID), the system must immediately trigger a Critical Identity Mismatch override. Automated processing is suspended, Review Priority is elevated to HIGH, Risk-Evidence Matrix is set to INVESTIGATE, and the application is routed for mandatory OFFICER_INVESTIGATION to prevent synthetic identity fraud.

chunks.description: Simulated demo rule governing applications with high historical rejection risk signals.
chunks.text: [SIMULATED DEMO RULE] Applications where the historical machine learning rejection-risk probability exceeds 65.0% (HIGH ML Risk level) must not be processed under standard underwriting pathways. Even if documentation is structurally complete, the application must be assigned to an experienced credit officer for OFFICER_INVESTIGATION to evaluate debt burden, risk factors, and secondary financial stability.

chunks.title: Simulated Bank Rule — Missing Mandatory Supporting Document Follow-up
chunks.section: Application Processing Part 5.1 — Document Package Completeness
chunks.description: Simulated demo rule specifying officer follow-up actions when mandatory documents are absent.
chunks.text: [SIMULATED DEMO RULE] If an application has missing mandatory supporting documents (such as Bank Statement or Tax Return) but exhibits no fraudulent identity mismatch, the application shall be categorized under Risk-Evidence Matrix category REVIEW with recommended action DOCUMENT_FOLLOWUP. The loan officer shall request the missing documentation from the applicant before rendering an underwriting decision.
chunks.applicability: All applications with document completeness status INCOMPLETE

chunks.title: Simulated Bank Rule — Salary Credit Reconciliation & Cash Deposit Policy
chunks.section: Underwriting Policy Part 2.4 — Salary Reconciliation & Cash Deposits
chunks.description: Simulated demo rule requiring salary credit correspondence and reconciliation for unverified cash deposits.
chunks.text: [SIMULATED DEMO RULE] Net monthly salary declared by the applicant must correspond directly with regular salary credit entries in the applicant's primary operational bank account statements. Any discrepancy exceeding standard deduction tolerances or unverified cash deposits requires reconciliation by underwriting.
chunks.applicability: All salaried loan applications
